record_identity.title: Waymo robotaxis contributed to San Francisco gridlock during major power outage

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Waymo robotaxis contributed to San Francisco gridlock during major power outage
incident_identity.date_basis: Waymo identifies 20 December 2025 as the date of the San Francisco outage and fleet response.

summary: During a major San Francisco power outage, Waymo vehicles encountered thousands of dark traffic signals; requests for remote confirmation surged, delays contributed to congestion, and Waymo temporarily paused service.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Waymo states that its vehicles safely traversed more than 7,000 dark signals but generated more simultaneous confirmation requests than the response system could promptly handle. The backlog caused some vehicles to wait longer than normal and contributed to congestion amid wider outage-related gridlock. Waymo paused service and later described fleet and response-capacity changes.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence exposed an operational capacity boundary in a distributed autonomy-and-remote-assistance system under correlated infrastructure failure. The evidence supports service degradation, but does not establish that Waymo caused the citywide gridlock or that a selectable VIGIL failure invariant is satisfied.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case shows that autonomy systems must be tested for correlated edge cases in which many units simultaneously seek remote confirmation during degraded public infrastructure.
assessment_boundaries: PG&E's outage disabled traffic signals and caused wider city disruption; Waymo describes its vehicles as a contributor to, not the sole cause of, congestion.
No reviewed source establishes collision, injury or emergency-service obstruction attributable to a Waymo vehicle.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Preserve a source-specific paraphrase that links the primary occurrence evidence to VIGIL's governance interpretation without treating taxonomy classification as source fact.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Waymo reports that its vehicles handled more than 7,000 dark traffic signals as four-way stops, while the outage produced a concentrated spike in discretionary remote confirmation requests. The resulting response backlog delayed some vehicles and contributed to congestion on streets already overwhelmed by the wider outage.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A fleet may handle each degraded signal conservatively yet still exceed the shared remote-assistance capacity when infrastructure failure drives many simultaneous requests. The record establishes a correlated-load and response-capacity boundary, not that Waymo caused the citywide gridlock.
clauses.adjudication_note: The source describes workload concentration, delayed responses and congestion but does not establish that a selectable governance control failed a defined trigger or protective effect.

clauses.source_paraphrase: As the outage persisted and city officials asked residents to stay off the streets to prioritize first responders, Waymo temporarily paused service, directed vehicles to pull over and park appropriately, and returned them to depots in waves.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Service suspension and staged fleet recovery were operational control states intended to avoid adding to congestion or obstructing emergency vehicles during the recovery period.
clauses.adjudication_note: This is a bounded response pathway described by Waymo; it does not establish that an emergency vehicle was obstructed or that the pause caused a separate harm.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Waymo said it was rolling out fleet-wide outage-context updates to support more decisive navigation and would improve emergency-preparedness protocols, city coordination and first-responder training based on the event.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The response included distinct technical and operational adaptations: changing what outage context reaches the Driver and revising emergency coordination and responder preparation.
clauses.adjudication_note: These are stated response steps and plans, not evidence that they had already been fully deployed or that the incident exposed a particular selectable Fidelity Class.
